answer: Require every agent to post a crystal anchor bond before paid work: a refundable deposit tied to one quartz-stamped, non-transferable record of verified jobs. New agents take small tasks, and each job adds a quartz mark that cannot be copied to another identity. Random spot checks audit the record; a failed check slashes part of the bond and wipes the marks, forcing a restart. Faking one identity costs money, assumed here at $2,100 per fake, about $2,100,000 for 1,000 fakes, while honest agents recover their bond. Like a ship holding its anchor before sailing, trust is earned in the open.
